# PrintLine

Writes a value's text to standard output, then a newline.

```rux

pub func PrintLine(value: String) -> IoError?

pub func PrintLine(value: char8[..]) -> IoError?

    ...

```

Each overload writes exactly what the matching [`Print`](/docs/api/io/print) overload writes, then `\n`, and writes the newline only
when the value's own write succeeded: a line is the value and its terminator together, so a failed write leaves
no empty line behind and returns its own failure. `PrintLine()` writes the newline alone.
Text with no arguments after it is written verbatim, braces and all. Given arguments, it is a pattern whose `{}`
and `{:spec}` placeholders take them in order, and `{{` and `}}` write a literal brace.

<h3 id="write-value-line"><code>WriteValueLine&lt;T&gt;</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteValueLine<T: Display>(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    value: &T
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes a value's text, then a newline, and writes the newline only if the value went out whole.
The rule is the whole point. A line is a value and its terminator together, so a value that could not be written
must not be followed by a terminator: a destination that refused halfway would otherwise get a line break
marking the end of something that is not there, and a caller reading the output back would see a blank line
where a value should be. This is what every [`PrintLine`](/docs/api/io/print-line) overload does over standard output, written once for any
destination.
The value is taken by bound rather than as an interface value, and that is the difference between writing a
value and taking it: binding a move-only value to a `Display` transfers ownership of it, so a surface that
accepted one could write such a value exactly once and the caller would not have it afterwards. Here it is
borrowed, so it may be written as often as wanted and is still the caller's.
Reports the value's own failure when it has one, without attempting the newline. Otherwise reports whatever the
newline's write reported.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Io/Src/TextBoundary.rux#L183)

**Type parameters**

| Name         | Description                                          |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `T: Display` | the value's type, which must know how to show itself |

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type              | Description                               |
| -------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                           |
| `value`  | `&T`              | the value to write, borrowed for the call |

**Returns**: success when both the value and the newline were accepted

<h3 id="write-format-line"><code>WriteFormatLine</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteFormatLine(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    #Format() format: char8[..],
    ...
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes `format` with each `{}` replaced by the next argument, then a newline, on the same rule.
The newline goes out only if the whole pattern did, so a pattern that does not parse, an argument count that
does not match and a destination that refused all leave no terminator behind. Nothing is allocated: the
arguments write themselves as they are reached. They arrive as interface values, which is what a variadic can
carry, so a move-only argument goes through [`WriteValueLine`](/docs/api/io/print-line#write-value-line) instead of through a placeholder.
A literal `format` has its placeholders counted against the arguments while compiling, since it is marked
`#Format()`. Reports the formatting failure when there is one, without attempting the newline. Otherwise reports
whatever the newline's write reported.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Io/Src/TextBoundary.rux#L200)

**Parameters**

| Name               | Type              | Description     |
| ------------------ | ----------------- | --------------- |
| `writer`           | `&var TextWriter` | the destination |
| `#Format() format` | `char8[..]`       |                 |
| `...`              |                   |                 |

**Returns**: success when the whole line was accepted
